title: Iron Mountain Secures Wind Power for Its Trio of Data Centers
summary: Iron Mountain has committed to powering its data centers entirely with renewable energy, signing a 15-year agreement for wind power in Pennsylvania. This move aligns the company with other mega-data center providers in prioritizing renewable sources, especially to serve major clients like Amazon and Microsoft, despite potential shifts in federal climate policy. The company projects that by 2018, solar and wind power will cover two-thirds of its North American electricity needs.

title: Here's What a $1,000 Investment in Amazon's 1997 Debut Is Worth Today
summary: This article examines the impressive growth of an early investment in Amazon.com Inc. since its 1997 IPO. It details how a $1,000 investment, despite early operating losses and multiple stock splits, would have grown to over half a million dollars by 2017 due to Amazon's aggressive expansion and market dominance. The piece highlights Amazon's journey from an online bookseller to a major e-commerce and tech giant, contrasting its performance with the broader retail sector.

title: Ralph Lauren Closing Fifth Avenue Polo Store, Cutting Staff
summary: Ralph Lauren Corp. is closing its Fifth Avenue Polo store in New York and reducing its corporate workforce as part of its "Way Forward Plan." These cost-cutting measures are expected to save approximately $140 million per year, though the restructuring will cost about $370 million. The company aims to optimize its store portfolio and shift its digital operations to a more flexible platform.

title: Amazon Alexa has become one of my BFFs, says Omnicom Media chief
summary: Omnicom Media Group's Philippa Brown highlights how Amazon's Alexa has transformed her work by enabling multitasking and streamlining daily tasks. She notes Alexa's continuous learning and expanding functionalities, impacting sectors like automotive, energy, and travel. Brown emphasizes the growing importance of voice-activated search for brands and anticipates significant developments, particularly in the automotive industry.

title: Amazon acquires stake in hydrogen fuel cell maker Plug Power, plans to spend $600M on batteries
summary: Amazon has secured the right to acquire a more than 20% stake in hydrogen fuel cell maker Plug Power, committing to spend $600 million on their products. This move aims to implement Plug Power's technology, including batteries for forklifts, in Amazon's fulfillment centers to improve efficiency and reduce maintenance. The deal highlights a growing trend among large retailers, including rival Walmart, to adopt hydrogen fuel cell technology for warehouse operations.

title: Plug Power Jumps Sharply After Reaching Deal With Amazon
summary: Shares of Plug Power (PLUG) surged by 63.5 percent after the company announced an agreement with Amazon (AMZN). This deal involves Plug Power providing fuel cells and hydrogen technology for Amazon's fulfillment network, leading to the stock's best intraday level in over a year.

title: Plug Power’s stock rockets after Amazon supply deal
summary: Plug Power's stock soared following news of a supply agreement with Amazon.com Inc. The deal, potentially worth up to $600 million, includes a significant equity investment and will see Amazon use Plug Power's fuel cells and hydrogen technology in its fulfillment network. Amazon plans to power industrial equipment, such as forklifts, with Plug Power’s GenKey technology.

title: The five-minute CIO: Dharmesh Shah, CTO, HubSpot
summary: Dharmesh Shah, co-founder and CTO of HubSpot, discusses the company's origins, its product development ethos, and the expansion of its European headquarters in Dublin. He highlights HubSpot's focus on creating intuitive software and its optimistic view on the future of AI and conversational user interfaces, particularly with the GrowthBot product. Shah also touches upon the challenges and successes of building a strong employer brand in Dublin and the technical hurdles of scaling their platform.

title: Google Espresso to boost delivery of cloud-based application services
summary: Google has introduced Espresso, a new peering architecture unveiled at the Open Networking Summit, designed to enhance the delivery of cloud-based application services from Google Cloud. Espresso improves application performance by expanding Google's software-defined networking infrastructure to the network edge and prioritizing traffic based on latency requirements. This system routes 20% of Google's immense internet traffic and replaces traditional routers with software-controlled switches for greater efficiency and reliability.

title: Amazon, Wal-Mart and Apple Top List of Biggest E-commerce Retailers
summary: Amazon, Apple, and Wal-Mart lead the list of top e-commerce retailers in the U.S. according to eMarketer data, with Amazon dominating online sales. While Amazon alone generated $94.7 billion in online sales, surpassing the combined total of the next 49 retailers, companies like Hudson's Bay Co. and Ulta Beauty showed significant e-commerce sales growth. The article also highlights how e-commerce profitability challenges affect traditional retailers.

title: OTT Breaks Out of Its Netflix Shell
summary: The article discusses the expansion of the Over-The-Top (OTT) streaming market beyond Netflix's initial dominance, driven by increasing adoption of TV-connected digital streaming devices. It highlights the growing presence of other services like YouTube, Amazon Video, and Hulu, noting that while Netflix leads in reach, other platforms are establishing strong footholds and attracting significant viewing hours. The piece suggests significant growth potential in the OTT market, particularly as many households have yet to engage with OTT services.

title: UPS Buys First Used Boeing 767s With New Ones Out of Reach
summary: UPS Inc. has purchased its first used Boeing 767s, three 767-300ER passenger aircraft, to be converted for cargo use. This move comes as new models are sold out and package shipments globally continue to increase. The company already operates 59 of these models and views this acquisition as an investment in capacity needed for growth.

title: Amazon's Third-Party Sellers Get Ripped Off By Hackers
summary: Hackers are targeting third-party Amazon sellers by taking over dormant accounts, changing bank information, and listing nonexistent merchandise to collect payments. This scam often leaves sellers, like Margina Dennis, in debt and fielding complaints from buyers who never receive their orders. Amazon acknowledges the issue and advises sellers to monitor accounts and use two-factor authentication, while experts suggest the company's current security measures may not be sufficient for the scale of the problem.

title: Fortinet upgrades for better cloud, SD-WAN protection
summary: Fortinet has released FortiOS 5.6, an upgraded operating system enabling unified security management across cloud assets and SD-WAN environments, including AWS and Azure. The company also announced FortiCASB, a platform for securing SaaS applications, which integrates with the Fortinet Security Fabric for consistent policy enforcement. These enhancements aim to provide comprehensive protection and simplified management for complex network infrastructures.

title: Garmin Vivosmart 3 now shipping
summary: The Garmin Vivosmart 3 fitness tracker is now shipping, featuring Elevate wrist heart-rate technology with 24/7 monitoring and VO2 maximum level determination. Priced at $139.99 USD, it also includes fitness age tracking, stress monitoring, smart notifications, and a battery life of up to five days. The device is available in black and purple from major retailers.

title: Troy Taylor Talks Coca-Cola Bottling, Distributing at Conversation With A CEO
summary: Troy Taylor, CEO of Coca-Cola Beverages Florida, shared his career journey and insights into entrepreneurship during a "Conversation with a CEO" event at the USF Muma College of Business. He advised aspiring entrepreneurs to gain experience and find their passion, recounting his 20-year path before starting his multi-billion dollar bottling and distribution company. Taylor also discussed the company's rapid growth, its commitment to sustainability and community giving, and the rich history of Coca-Cola bottling.

title: Yext finishes the day up 21% as IPO window remains wide open
summary: Yext, a company specializing in location data for businesses, went public on the NYSE, with its stock rising 21% on its first day of trading. The IPO raised $115.5 million, which Yext plans to invest in sales and marketing as it eyes international expansion and evolving into a "knowledge engine." This successful IPO highlights a re-opened window for tech IPOs, following other companies like Snapchat parent Snap, MuleSoft, Alteryx, and Okta.

title: BJ’s Wholesale Club up for sale and Amazon may be interested
summary: BJ’s Wholesale Club is reportedly for sale, with private equity owners CVC Capital Partners and Leonard Green & Partners seeking over $4 billion. Amazon has shown modest internal interest in the acquisition, which could help its brick-and-mortar expansion and Amazon Fresh delivery service. The owners are set for a significant return on their 2011 investment, despite analyst concerns about BJ's competitive standing.

title: Cable Vet Kathy Payne Joins Amazon’s Ranks as Channels Content Executive
summary: Kathy Payne, a veteran programming executive from Suddenlink Communications and Cox Communications, has joined Amazon as head of content acquisition for Amazon Channels. Her extensive experience in negotiating carriage deals, particularly with major content providers, suggests Amazon may be looking to expand its Amazon Channels offering to include more traditional pay TV services. Industry analysts believe this hire could signal Amazon's strategic move into becoming an OTT distributor of linear television programming.

title: Walmart's Push to Boost Online Fashion Presence With Acquisitions
summary: Walmart is actively acquiring small online fashion and accessories brands, such as Bonobos, ShoeBuy, Moosejaw, and ModCloth, to boost its online presence and compete with Amazon. This strategy aims to capture younger, millennial customers and expand its online sales growth, despite past struggles in the e-commerce sector. The company expects continued acquisitions spearheaded by Marc Lore to rapidly grow its online business.

title: Netflix's biggest competitor? Sleep
summary: Netflix CEO Reed Hastings claims the company's biggest competitor is human sleep, not other streaming services. This article explores how tech giants like Netflix, Uber, and Facebook redefine their competition, often looking beyond direct rivals to fundamental user behaviors or future technological advancements. It suggests that while these companies articulate unusual competitive landscapes, their day-to-day efforts often remain focused on traditional rivals.

title: Procter & Gamble names Coke IT vet as new CIO
summary: Procter & Gamble has announced Javier Polit, formerly of The Coca-Cola Company, as its new CIO, replacing Linda Clement-Holmes. Polit is expected to accelerate the business application of IT capability and strengthen the IT function, leveraging his experience in mobile applications, IoT, and analytics. This move comes as consumer packaged goods companies increasingly look to digital strategies to connect with consumers.

title: Report: CVS says time for more healthy options, less candy, at checkout counter
summary: CVS Health Corp. is implementing a new store format focusing on healthier options and health products, reducing candy and other general merchandise from checkout areas and other parts of its stores. This redesign, already introduced in 800 of its 9,700 stores, aims to boost sales and aligns with the company's broader focus on health care, following its previous decision to abandon tobacco sales. The company plans to roll out this format to several hundred more stores by the end of next year.

title: Nomura collaborates with PwC, Google, IBM, and Amazon for fintech project in India
summary: Nomura has launched "Voyager- Nomura Fintech Partnership" in India, a collaborative project with PwC, Google, IBM, and Amazon, to develop fintech solutions for capital markets and investment banking. The initiative, run through the Nomura Innovation Centre (NICe) in Mumbai, aims to enlist entrepreneurs and start-ups to create innovative solutions, providing them with access to Nomura's resources and potentially securing Nomura as a client or investor. This move further signifies Nomura's commitment to financial innovation and engagement with start-ups, building on its existing global fintech initiatives and plans for a 10 billion yen fund for start-ups.

title: Casey Carl, Target's innovation chief, is leaving
summary: Casey Carl, Target's chief innovation and strategy officer, is leaving the company as CEO Brian Cornell refocuses on core business operations. His departure comes as Target dismantles several experimental projects he championed, including a store-of-the-future concept. The retailer is shifting its strategy towards remodeling stores, lowering prices, and launching new in-house brands to revitalize sales amidst fierce competition.

title: How Bill O’Reilly Leaving Fox Fired Up O’Reilly Auto Parts Stock
summary: Following news of Bill O'Reilly's departure from Fox News, O’Reilly Automotive (ORLY) stock unexpectedly rose. This surge is theorized to be due to computerized trading algorithms misinterpreting social media chatter about Bill O'Reilly as a signal to buy shares of the unrelated auto parts company. The incident highlights potential flaws in social sentiment-based investing, drawing parallels to previous algorithmic errors involving Anne Hathaway and Lululemon.

title: Amazon blazes a trail to the next frontier in AI: the cloud
summary: Amazon is making a significant push into artificial intelligence, particularly by leveraging its AWS cloud to democratize machine learning for developers. CEO Jeff Bezos views machine learning as crucial for the company's future, powering internal operations and customer-facing services like Alexa and Amazon Go, and setting Amazon up as a platform company in AI. The company is focusing on making deep learning accessible, supporting various frameworks, and addressing scalability challenges for petabytes of data.

title: T.J. Maxx, Marshalls in talks to bring distribution facility with 1,000 jobs to San Antonio
summary: TJX Companies Inc., the parent company of T.J. Maxx and Marshalls, is in negotiations to build a $150 million distribution center on San Antonio's South Side. This facility is expected to create at least 1,000 jobs in the area. Local officials and the Southside Independent School District have been involved in discussions, with the school district already approving tax incentives for an unnamed company.

title: JD.com announces the establishment of JD Logistics - Transport Intelligence
summary: JD.com has announced the establishment of JD Logistics, a new business group leveraging the company's technology to provide supply chain and logistics services across various industries. Zhenhui Wang will serve as CEO, reporting to Richard Liu, Chairman and CEO of JD.com. The new entity aims to revolutionize China’s commercial infrastructure using AI, big data, and automation, offering warehousing, transportation, delivery, after-sales, and cross-border logistics services.
